clauses.normalized_text: A QUIC stream provides reliable in-order delivery of bytes, within that stream.
clauses.raw_text: A QUIC stream provides reliable in-order delivery of bytes, within that stream.

clauses.normalized_text: On the wire, data is framed into QUIC STREAM frames, but this framing is invisible to the HTTP/2 layer.
clauses.raw_text: On the wire, data is framed into QUIC STREAM frames, but this framing is invisible to the HTTP/2 layer.

clauses.normalized_text: A QUIC receiver buffers and orders received STREAM frames, exposing the data contained within as a reliable byte stream to the application.
clauses.raw_text: A QUIC receiver buffers and orders received STREAM frames, exposing the data contained within as a reliable byte stream to the application.

clauses.normalized_text: Bytes written to Stream 3 must be HTTP/2 HEADERS frames (or other HTTP/2 non-data frames), whereas bytes written to data streams should simply be request or response bodies.
clauses.raw_text: Bytes written to Stream 3 must be HTTP/2 HEADERS frames (or other HTTP/2 non-data frames), whereas bytes written to data streams should simply be request or response bodies.

clauses.normalized_text: No further framing is required by HTTP/2 (i.e. no HTTP/2 DATA frames are used).
clauses.raw_text: No further framing is required by HTTP/2 (i.e. no HTTP/2 DATA frames are used).

clauses.normalized_text: If data arrives on a data stream before the corresponding HEADERS have arrived on stream 3, then the data is buffered until the HEADERS arrive.
clauses.raw_text: If data arrives on a data stream before the corresponding HEADERS have arrived on stream 3, then the data is buffered until the HEADERS arrive.

clauses.normalized_text: When HTTP/2 headers and data are sent over QUIC, the QUIC layer handles most of the stream management.
clauses.raw_text: When HTTP/2 headers and data are sent over QUIC, the QUIC layer handles most of the stream management.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2 StreamIDs are replaced by QUIC StreamIDs.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2 StreamIDs are replaced by QUIC StreamIDs.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2 does not need to do any explicit stream framing when using QUIC - data sent over a QUIC stream simply consists of HTTP/2 headers or body.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2 does not need to do any explicit stream framing when using QUIC - data sent over a QUIC stream simply consists of HTTP/2 headers or body.

clauses.normalized_text: Requests and responses are considered complete when the QUIC stream is closed in the corresponding direction.
clauses.raw_text: Requests and responses are considered complete when the QUIC stream is closed in the corresponding direction.

clauses.normalized_text: Like HTTP/2, QUIC uses odd-numbered StreamIDs for client initiated streams, and even-numbered IDs for server initiated (i.e. server push) streams.
clauses.raw_text: Like HTTP/2, QUIC uses odd-numbered StreamIDs for client initiated streams, and even-numbered IDs for server initiated (i.e. server push) streams.

clauses.normalized_text: Unlike HTTP/2 there are a couple of reserved (or dedicated) StreamIDs in QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: Unlike HTTP/2 there are a couple of reserved (or dedicated) StreamIDs in QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: StreamID 1 is reserved for crypto operations (the handshake, crypto config updates), and MUST NOT be used for HTTP/2 headers or body, see [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
clauses.raw_text: StreamID 1 is reserved for crypto operations (the handshake, crypto config updates), and MUST NOT be used for HTTP/2 headers or body, see [QUIC-TRANSPORT].

clauses.normalized_text: StreamID 3 is reserved for sending and receiving HTTP/2 HEADERS frames.
clauses.raw_text: StreamID 3 is reserved for sending and receiving HTTP/2 HEADERS frames.

clauses.normalized_text: Therefore the first client initiated data stream has StreamID 5.
clauses.raw_text: Therefore the first client initiated data stream has StreamID 5.

clauses.normalized_text: There are no reserved server initiated StreamIDs, so the first server initiated (i.e. server push) stream has an ID of 2, followed by 4, etc.
clauses.raw_text: There are no reserved server initiated StreamIDs, so the first server initiated (i.e. server push) stream has an ID of 2, followed by 4, etc.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2-over-QUIC uses HPACK header compression as described in [RFC7541].
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2-over-QUIC uses HPACK header compression as described in [RFC7541].

clauses.normalized_text: HPACK was designed for HTTP/2 with the assumption of in- order delivery such as that provided by TCP.
clauses.raw_text: HPACK was designed for HTTP/2 with the assumption of in- order delivery such as that provided by TCP.

clauses.normalized_text: A sequence of encoded header blocks must arrive (and be decoded) at an endpoint in the same order in which they were encoded.
clauses.raw_text: A sequence of encoded header blocks must arrive (and be decoded) at an endpoint in the same order in which they were encoded.

clauses.normalized_text: This ensures that the dynamic state at the two endpoints remains in sync.
clauses.raw_text: This ensures that the dynamic state at the two endpoints remains in sync.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC streams provide in-order delivery of data sent on those streams, but there are no guarantees about order of delivery between streams.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC streams provide in-order delivery of data sent on those streams, but there are no guarantees about order of delivery between streams.

clauses.normalized_text: To achieve in-order delivery of HEADERS frames in QUIC, they are all sent on the reserved Stream 3.
clauses.raw_text: To achieve in-order delivery of HEADERS frames in QUIC, they are all sent on the reserved Stream 3.

clauses.normalized_text: Data (request/response bodies) which arrive on other data streams are buffered until the corresponding HEADERS arrive and are read out of Stream 3.
clauses.raw_text: Data (request/response bodies) which arrive on other data streams are buffered until the corresponding HEADERS arrive and are read out of Stream 3.

clauses.normalized_text: This does introduce head-of-line blocking: if the packet containing HEADERS for stream N is lost or reordered then stream N+2 cannot be processed until they it has been retransmitted successfully, even though the HEADERS for stream N+2 may have arrived.
clauses.raw_text: This does introduce head-of-line blocking: if the packet containing HEADERS for stream N is lost or reordered then stream N+2 cannot be processed until they it has been retransmitted successfully, even though the HEADERS for stream N+2 may have arrived.

clauses.normalized_text: Trailing headers (trailers) can also be sent on stream 3.
clauses.raw_text: Trailing headers (trailers) can also be sent on stream 3.

clauses.normalized_text: These are sent as HTTP/2 HEADERS frames, but MUST have the END_STREAM bit set, and MUST include a “:final-offset” pseudo-header.
clauses.raw_text: These are sent as HTTP/2 HEADERS frames, but MUST have the END_STREAM bit set, and MUST include a “:final-offset” pseudo-header.

clauses.normalized_text: Since QUIC supports out of order delivery, receipt of a HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM bit set does not guarantee that the entire request/ response body has been fully received.
clauses.raw_text: Since QUIC supports out of order delivery, receipt of a HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM bit set does not guarantee that the entire request/ response body has been fully received.

clauses.normalized_text: Therefore, the extra “:final-offset” pseudo-header is included in trailing HEADERS frames to indicate the total number of body bytes sent on the corresponding data stream.
clauses.raw_text: Therefore, the extra “:final-offset” pseudo-header is included in trailing HEADERS frames to indicate the total number of body bytes sent on the corresponding data stream.

clauses.normalized_text: This is used by the QUIC layer to determine when the full request has been received and therefore when it is safe to tear down local stream state.

clauses.normalized_text: The “:final-offset” pseudo header is stripped from the HEADERS before passing to the HTTP/2 layer.
clauses.raw_text: The “:final-offset” pseudo header is stripped from the HEADERS before passing to the HTTP/2 layer.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2-over-QUIC uses the HTTP/2 priority scheme described in [RFC7540] Section 5.3.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2-over-QUIC uses the HTTP/2 priority scheme described in [RFC7540] Section 5.3.

clauses.normalized_text: In the HTTP/2 priority scheme, a given stream can be designated as dependent upon another stream, which expresses the preference that the latter stream (the “parent” stream) be allocated resources before the former stream (the “dependent” stream).
clauses.raw_text: In the HTTP/2 priority scheme, a given stream can be designated as dependent upon another stream, which expresses the preference that the latter stream (the “parent” stream) be allocated resources before the former stream (the “dependent” stream).

clauses.normalized_text: Taken together, the dependencies across all streams in a connection form a dependency tree.
clauses.raw_text: Taken together, the dependencies across all streams in a connection form a dependency tree.

clauses.normalized_text: The structure of the dependency tree changes as HTTP/2 HEADERS and PRIORITY frames add, remove, or change the dependency links between streams.
clauses.raw_text: The structure of the dependency tree changes as HTTP/2 HEADERS and PRIORITY frames add, remove, or change the dependency links between streams.

clauses.normalized_text: Implicit in this scheme is the notion of in-order delivery of priority changes (i.e., dependency tree mutations): since operations on the dependency tree such as reparenting a subtree are not commutative, both sender and receiver must apply them in the same order to ensure that both sides have a consistent view of the stream dependency tree.
clauses.raw_text: Implicit in this scheme is the notion of in-order delivery of priority changes (i.e., dependency tree mutations): since operations on the dependency tree such as reparenting a subtree are not commutative, both sender and receiver must apply them in the same order to ensure that both sides have a consistent view of the stream dependency tree.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2 specifies priority assignments in PRIORITY frames and (optionally) in HEADERS frames.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2 specifies priority assignments in PRIORITY frames and (optionally) in HEADERS frames.

clauses.normalized_text: To achieve in-order delivery of HTTP/2 priority changes in HTTP/2-over-QUIC, HTTP/2 PRIORITY frames, in addition to HEADERS frames, are also sent on reserved stream 3.
clauses.raw_text: To achieve in-order delivery of HTTP/2 priority changes in HTTP/2-over-QUIC, HTTP/2 PRIORITY frames, in addition to HEADERS frames, are also sent on reserved stream 3.

clauses.normalized_text: The semantics of the Stream Dependency, Weight, E flag, and (for HEADERS frames) PRIORITY flag are the same as in HTTP/2-over-TCP.
clauses.raw_text: The semantics of the Stream Dependency, Weight, E flag, and (for HEADERS frames) PRIORITY flag are the same as in HTTP/2-over-TCP.

clauses.normalized_text: Since HEADERS and PRIORITY frames are sent on a different stream than the STREAM frames for the streams they reference, they may be delivered out-of-order with respect to the STREAM frames.
clauses.raw_text: Since HEADERS and PRIORITY frames are sent on a different stream than the STREAM frames for the streams they reference, they may be delivered out-of-order with respect to the STREAM frames.

clauses.normalized_text: There is no special handling for this–the receiver should simply assign resources according to the most recent stream priority information that it has received.
clauses.raw_text: There is no special handling for this–the receiver should simply assign resources according to the most recent stream priority information that it has received.

clauses.raw_text: ALTERNATIVE DESIGN: if the core QUIC protocol implements priorities, then this document should map the HTTP/2 priorities scheme to that provided by the core protocol.

clauses.normalized_text: This would likely involve prohibiting the sending of HTTP/2 PRIORITY frames and setting of the PRIORITY flag in HTTP/2 HEADERS frames, to avoid conflicting directives.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC provides stream and connection level flow control, similar in principle to HTTP/2’s flow control but with some implementation differences.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC provides stream and connection level flow control, similar in principle to HTTP/2’s flow control but with some implementation differences.

clauses.normalized_text: As flow control is handled by QUIC, the HTTP/2 mapping need not concern itself with maintaining flow control state, or how/ when to send flow control frames to the peer.
clauses.raw_text: As flow control is handled by QUIC, the HTTP/2 mapping need not concern itself with maintaining flow control state, or how/ when to send flow control frames to the peer.

clauses.normalized_text: The HTTP/2 mapping must not send HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE frames.
clauses.raw_text: The HTTP/2 mapping must not send HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE frames.

clauses.normalized_text: The initial flow control window sizes (stream and connection) are communicated during the crypto handshake (see [connection-establishment]).
clauses.raw_text: The initial flow control window sizes (stream and connection) are communicated during the crypto handshake (see [connection-establishment]).

clauses.normalized_text: Setting these values to the maximum size (2^31 - 1) effectively disables flow control.
clauses.raw_text: Setting these values to the maximum size (2^31 - 1) effectively disables flow control.

clauses.normalized_text: Relatively small initial windows can be used, as QUIC will attempt to auto-tune the flow control windows based on usage.
clauses.raw_text: Relatively small initial windows can be used, as QUIC will attempt to auto-tune the flow control windows based on usage.

clauses.raw_text: See [QUIC-TRANSPORT] for more details.

clauses.normalized_text: HTTP/2-over-QUIC supports HTTP/2 server push.
clauses.raw_text: HTTP/2-over-QUIC supports HTTP/2 server push.

clauses.normalized_text: During connection establishment, the client indicates whether or it is willing to receive server pushes via the SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH setting in the HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame (see [connection-establishment]), which defaults to 1 (true).
clauses.raw_text: During connection establishment, the client indicates whether or it is willing to receive server pushes via the SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH setting in the HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame (see [connection-establishment]), which defaults to 1 (true).

clauses.normalized_text: As with server push for HTTP/2-over-TCP, the server initiates a server push by sending an HTTP/2 PUSH_PROMISE frame containing the StreamID of the stream to be pushed, as well as request header fields attributed to the request.
clauses.raw_text: As with server push for HTTP/2-over-TCP, the server initiates a server push by sending an HTTP/2 PUSH_PROMISE frame containing the StreamID of the stream to be pushed, as well as request header fields attributed to the request.

clauses.normalized_text: The PUSH_PROMISE frame is sent on stream 3, to ensure proper ordering with respect to other HEADERS and non- data frames.
clauses.raw_text: The PUSH_PROMISE frame is sent on stream 3, to ensure proper ordering with respect to other HEADERS and non- data frames.

clauses.normalized_text: Within the PUSH_PROMISE frame, the StreamID in the common HTTP/2 frame header indicates the associated (client- initiated) stream for the new push stream, while the Promised Stream ID field specifies the StreamID of the new push stream.
clauses.raw_text: Within the PUSH_PROMISE frame, the StreamID in the common HTTP/2 frame header indicates the associated (client- initiated) stream for the new push stream, while the Promised Stream ID field specifies the StreamID of the new push stream.

clauses.normalized_text: The server push response is conveyed in the same way as a non-server- push response, with response headers and (if present) trailers carried by HTTP/2 HEADERS frames sent on reserved stream 3, and response body (if any) sent via QUIC stream frames on the stream specified in the corresponding PUSH_PROMISE frame.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC includes some features (e.g. flow control) which are also present in HTTP/2.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC includes some features (e.g. flow control) which are also present in HTTP/2.

clauses.normalized_text: In these cases the HTTP/2 mapping need not re- implement them.
clauses.raw_text: In these cases the HTTP/2 mapping need not re- implement them.

clauses.normalized_text: As a result some HTTP/2 frame types are not required when using QUIC, as they either are directly implemented in the QUIC layer, or their functionality is provided via other means.
clauses.raw_text: As a result some HTTP/2 frame types are not required when using QUIC, as they either are directly implemented in the QUIC layer, or their functionality is provided via other means.

clauses.normalized_text: This section of the document describes these cases.
clauses.raw_text: This section of the document describes these cases.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC has its own GOAWAY frame, and QUIC implementations may to expose the sending of a GOAWAY to the application.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC has its own GOAWAY frame, and QUIC implementations may to expose the sending of a GOAWAY to the application.

clauses.normalized_text: The semantics of sending a GOAWAY in QUIC are identical to HTTP/2: an endpoint sending a GOAWAY will continue processing open streams, but will not accept newly created streams.
clauses.raw_text: The semantics of sending a GOAWAY in QUIC are identical to HTTP/2: an endpoint sending a GOAWAY will continue processing open streams, but will not accept newly created streams.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s GOAWAY frame is described in detail in the [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s GOAWAY frame is described in detail in the [QUIC-TRANSPORT].

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC has its own PING frame, which is currently exposed to the application.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC has its own PING frame, which is currently exposed to the application.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC clients send periodic PINGs to servers if there are no currently active data streams on the connection.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC clients send periodic PINGs to servers if there are no currently active data streams on the connection.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC’s PING frame is described in detail in the [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
clauses.raw_text: QUIC’s PING frame is described in detail in the [QUIC-TRANSPORT].

clauses.normalized_text: There is no HTTP/2 padding in this mapping; padding is instead provided at the QUIC layer by including QUIC PADDING frames in a packet payload.
clauses.raw_text: There is no HTTP/2 padding in this mapping; padding is instead provided at the QUIC layer by including QUIC PADDING frames in a packet payload.

clauses.normalized_text: An HTTP/2 over QUIC mapping should treat any HTTP/2 level padding as an error, to avoid any possibility of inconsistent flow control states between endpoints (e.g. client sends HTTP/2 padding, counts it against flow control, server ignores).
clauses.raw_text: An HTTP/2 over QUIC mapping should treat any HTTP/2 level padding as an error, to avoid any possibility of inconsistent flow control states between endpoints (e.g. client sends HTTP/2 padding, counts it against flow control, server ignores).

clauses.normalized_text: The security considerations of HTTP over QUIC should be comparable to those of HTTP/2.
clauses.raw_text: The security considerations of HTTP over QUIC should be comparable to those of HTTP/2.
